scope: Theorem 3.2 (Local estimate with variation in depth) of the manuscript “Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations” (preprints/Pointwise-convergence-of-triple-ergodic-averages-for-mixing-transformations-October-4-2026/pointwise-triple-ergodic-averages-mixing-transformations.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e76fd7732f10b250), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix the admissibility parameters c0, C0. Let J be an interval in any dyadic lattice, let T be a finite rooted tree below J, and let d be its largest depth in J. Let I ⊆ T , with an admissible kernel on each of its intervals. For each j ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3}, let fj,s : J → C, 0 ≤ s ≤ d, be measurable, and write fj = (fj,s)d s=0. Suppose that {0, . . . , d} is partitioned into Wj ≥ 1 deterministic nonempty consecutive blocks and that, on every block B, VB(fj)(y) ≤ W −1/2 j for almost every y ∈ J. The four partitions may differ. Extend the inputs by zero outside J. Then X I∈I |I| HI(f0,s(I), f1,s(I), f2,s(I), f3,s(I)) ≤ Cloc(c0, C0)|J|. (3.1) The constant is independent of the lattice, root, tree, kernels, depth range, blocks, and their numbers.
